proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 5127 reaches 1 in fewer than 113 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 50, the stopping time of n is less than 113.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 5127, the stopping time of n is less than 113.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 85 modulo 5.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000 for which n^2 > 2000.
The steps above establish the statement up to 5127, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 5127.
